ai.description: *Sitana laticeps* is a small lizard (SVL ~50 mm) with a broad head. It is brown with a series of dark rhomboidal dorsal spots and a distinct, colorful, multi-scaled gular fan in males.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Sitana laticeps* is its significantly broader head and the presence of a distinct, deep black patch on the gular fold.
ai.habitat: *Sitana laticeps* inhabits dry, open scrublands and rocky areas within the Deccan Plateau, typically found at low to moderate elevations in sparse, deciduous vegetation.
ai.behavior: During the breeding season, males perform conspicuous displays by rapidly extending and retracting their vibrant, fan-like throat pouches to attract mates and deter rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sitana laticeps* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–7 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sitana laticeps* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily inhabiting the Deccan Plateau and the Eastern Ghats at elevations ranging from near sea level to 800 meters.
